cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Greatness – the quality of being great; distinction or eminence.

p.em: Example: Striving for artistic greatness requires immense sacrifice.

cosy-blockquote.p: Haunting – poignant and evocative; difficult to forget.

p.em: Example: Her haunting vocal melody stayed in the audience's mind.

cosy-blockquote.p: Surrender – the action of surrendering or yielding to force.

p.em: Example: She refused to surrender her vision to corporate pressure.

cosy-blockquote.p: Struggle – a forceful effort to overcome obstacles.

p.em: Example: The struggle for creative independence defines every artist.

cosy-blockquote.p: Release – the action of setting free or releasing.

p.em: Example: Music provides a cathartic release from inner tension.

cosy-blockquote.p: Echo – a detail that recalls or resembles something else.

p.em: Example: Her voice echoed through the ancient stone amphitheater.

cosy-blockquote.p: Wilderness – an uncultivated, uninhabited, and wild region.

p.em: Example: Walking through the creative wilderness can feel lonely.

cosy-blockquote.p: Triumph – a great victory or achievement.

p.em: Example: Achieving recognition after years of quiet work was a triumph.

cosy-blockquote.p: Legacy – something handed down from an ancestor or predecessor.

p.em: Example: She wanted to build a musical legacy that inspires future generations.

cosy-blockquote.p: Grace – smoothness and elegance of movement or behavior.

p.em: Example: Handling harsh criticism with quiet grace defines true mastery.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: To be one of the greats, you have prepare → Correct: To be one of the greats, you have to prepare ((Include 'to' in obligation modal 'have to + verb'.))
Incorrect: She was one of the great → Correct: She was one of the greats ((Use plural noun 'greats' when referring to distinguished individuals.))
Incorrect: Her voice echoed through → Correct: Her voice echoed across ((Preposition 'through' or 'across' accurately describes sound reverberation.))
